title: Who are the Cabinet members of BARMM chief Macacua’s admin?
summary: The newly constituted Cabinet brings a mix of veteran lawmakers, technocrats, and legal professionals to lead the region's ministries and offices

blocks.text: CABINET. BARMM Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua announces on November 5, 2026 the newly constituted Cabinet of his administration, marking what he hailed as a "defining moment" in Bangsamoro history.
The newly constituted Cabinet brings a mix of veteran lawmakers, technocrats, and legal professionals to lead the region's ministries and offices

COTABATO CITY, Philippines – Following the historic inauguration of the region’s first-ever elected parliament, Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua officially announced on Thursday, November 5 the newly constituted Cabinet of his administration, marking what he hailed as a “defining moment” in Bangsamoro history.

The announcement comes on the heels of a vetting and screening process conducted by a special committee, designed to select leaders based on “competence, professional experience, integrity, and a strict commitment to moral governance.”
“To my fellow Bangsamoro, this government is yours,” Macacua declared. “We will pursue a policy of moral governance, integrity, and accountability.”

blocks.caption: Macacua is BARMM Parliament’s first elected chief minister | The wRap

blocks.text: The newly constituted Cabinet brings a mix of veteran lawmakers, technocrats, and legal professionals to lead the region’s ministries and offices:

items: Senior Minister: Member of Parliament (MP) Abunawas Maslamama
Bangsamoro Attorney-General’s Office: Judge Duque D. Kadatuan
Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education: MP Atty. Naguib G. Sinarimbo
Ministry of Social Services and Development: Atty. Alirakim Munder
Ministry of Health: MP Atty. Jimael Salam D. Salliman
Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform: MP Atty. Ishak V. Mastura
Ministry of Interior and Local Government: Jordan S. Bayam
Ministry of Public Order and Safety: Datu Jomar U. Midtimbang
Ministry of Labor and Employment: MP Atty. Kitem D. Kadatuan, Jr.
Ministry of Trade and Investment, and Tourism: Atty. Faizal M. Padate
Ministry of Indigenous People’s Affair: MP Jo Genna Jover
Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management: Atty. Ubaida C. Pacasem
Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources, and Energy: MP Akmad Brahim
Ministry of Science and Technology: MP Hanie Bud
Ministry of Human Settlement and Development: MP Engr. Rashdi T. Adiong
Ministry of Transportation and Communication: Termizie G. Masahud
Ministry of Public Works: Engr. Basir M. Ibrahim

blocks.text: Macacua acknowledged that the governance workload ahead is immense, but emphasized that the regional leadership’s resolve remains even greater. He underscored the administration’s dedication to preserving the hard-won gains of the peace process.

“We commit to sustaining the gains of the peace process and ensuring that the dividends of autonomy are felt in every household and every community,” Macacua said. “Together, with the continued support of our national government, local government units, and our partners, we will write a new chapter of peace, prosperity, and dignity for our people.”

Reflecting on the big tasks ahead, Macacua underscored that the newly formed administration will vigorously pursue moral governance—the foundational policy initiated by former chief minister Al Haj Murad Ebrahim.

“My fellow Bangsamoro, this government is yours,” Macacua stated. “We will pursue and vanish your moral or moral governance that had been initiated by former chief minister Al Haj Murad Ebrahim. Indeed, the work ahead is immense, but our resolve is greater.”
Macacua also committed his administration to sustaining the ongoing peace process and ensuring that the tangible dividends of regional autonomy reach every household and community.

He also expressed gratitude for the continued, collaborative backing of the national government, inter-governmental units, and international and local partners in cultivating peace, prosperity, and dignity for the Bangsamoro land and its people. – Rappler.com
